english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies from 7th July 2026 due to changes made by the National Security (State Threats) Act 2026. For the offence applying after this date, see H102840.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023.
(iii) This offence covers 'espionage' in the form of obtaining or disclosing of protected information in relation to the government’s sensitive information (information such as defence information or the work of intelligence agencies). For espionage relating to the disclosure of trade secrets, see H101392. For the offence relating to assisting a foreign intelligence service, see H101393 (conduct 'intended' to assist) and H101394 (conduct 'likely to assist').
(iv) The term "safety or interests of the UK" is not defined by the legislation but case-law has interpreted it as meaning the objects of state policy determined by the Crown on the advice of Ministers, Chandler v DPP.
(v) The person's conduct must meet the "foreign power condition" as set out in section 31.
(vi) Section 1(3) provides that the offence captures conduct both in the UK or elsewhere. Practically, this means that the offence may apply to UK personnel working for the Government abroad, locally engaged staff working for the Government abroad and/or people who use cyber means to access protected information remotely.
(vii) For the purposes of this section a person retains protected information if the person retains it in their possession or under their control; and disclosure includes parting with possession, section 1(5).
(viii) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
